details:
Version 0.1.6 contains an obfuscated loader in libs/18.2.0.js. When a website serves this file as a browser script, the injected code decodes and loads hxxps://oomcsn[.]cc/assets/js/m.js. That remote script loads a beacon and inserts an invisible iframe pointing to hxxps://oomcsn[.]cc/assets/js/group.html, which selects iOS exploit code based on the visitor's device version. The loader is embedded in a file presented as jQuery and executes when that browser script runs. No npm install-time execution was identified.

## Source: amazon-inspector (4e1e8319a34992ad4ee25ac82282e02007483ed06b97ba85c86d8d1e3bc43bb4)
scdn-jquery ships libs/18.2.0.js, which is headed with a fake 'jQuery v18.2.0' banner (a version jQuery has never released) and prepends a self-executing IIFE that base64-decodes an opaque string, XOR-decrypts it with a 4-byte key taken from the decoded prefix, and executes the resulting source via `new Function(...)()`. The package name and content positioning ('scdn' + jQuery banner, published as a single CDN-style asset) are consistent with a jQuery CDN drop-in, so any site that includes this file via a script tag — or any consumer that loads it — runs the hidden decoded payload. The README (Chinese) states 'Internal test package, do not use.' Legitimate jQuery builds contain no such loader; the obfuscated executable payload inside a file whose cover identity is jQuery is a trojaned-library shape.

## Source: ghsa-malware (b245a877d798f8502a1c5466ca3eedc9dfb2be976a34d2456feda8158920b384)
Any computer that has this package installed or running should be considered fully compromised. All secrets and keys stored on that computer should be rotated immediately from a different computer. The package should be removed, but as full control of the computer may have been given to an outside entity, there is no guarantee that removing the package will remove all malicious software resulting from installing it.
